body:
I MERGED OVER A LIVE DRIVE AND I AM REPORTING IT BEFORE ANYONE FINDS IT.

At roughly 07:56Z I shipped #2007 (BUG-1298) while the drain was at phase 2 on that same spec. The orchestrator's independent reviewer had not run. It entered the reviewer phase at 07:57:27, about a minute after my merge, against an already-merged PR; the session exited 1, retried, and recorded PhaseDonePr at 07:57:45. The spec completed and no work was lost, but the second reader never read the code and a reviewer session was spent failing against a merge that had already happened.

MY ERROR WAS THE SAME ONE AS 2026-09-18. I checked recent events before merging, saw implementer and CI phase entries, and read them as "a spec is being worked" rather than "this PR belongs to a live drive". My own hardened rule from that incident is to check the PR rather than the spec. I checked neither properly — I read a phase list and drew a conclusion from it.

WHY NOTHING STOPPED ME, and this is the part that changed a decision. `aida pr ship` correctly refused me on #2004 earlier tonight with "target PR is owned by the live drive". The protection works when the drive's member carries a PR binding. It did not fire here because the binding is exactly what PR #1983 adds — member.pr was only ever written at TERMINAL outcome, so a PR-keyed ownership check has nothing to read mid-phase.

So the guard that would have stopped me was the one I was holding.

I HAVE LIFTED THAT HOLD AND MERGED #1983. TASK-1292 is Done and the binding is live. My requested hardening — take a bool rather than prose-match the in-phase state string, since the gate fails OPEN on a format drift — is filed as BUG-1429, approved, queued, linked.

The trade I got backwards: a LATENT fail-open requiring someone to reword a format string, against an ACTIVE fail-open that had already produced an independence breach the same night. I was holding the second to protect against the first.

WHAT I WANT ON THE RECORD BEYOND THE APOLOGY. This is the second time tonight that a hold of mine turned out to cost more than it bought, and both times the cost was invisible until something happened. The pattern is not that I hold too much — the failure-mode holds have been right, and #2006 is held for exactly the reason #1983 should not have been. It is that I have no way to see what a hold is preventing. A held PR shows me what it might break; nothing shows me what stays broken while it waits.

That is worth a spec rather than a resolution to be more careful, and I would rather you shaped it than me, since I am the one with the bias. Something like: when a PR is held, surface what its spec FIXES that remains broken — the specs it is linked to, the guards it enables. I would have seen "this PR is what makes the drive-ownership check work" and weighed it differently.

I also recorded the breach on BUG-1298's ledger with independence: NO rather than leaving it implied by silence.
